answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering works by hashing each identity's device and timing signatures into a shared ledger; duplicate agents inherit overlapping clusters, so a copied identity's activity pattern will whisper its origin to verifiers. Any new cluster entry must clear a velvet threshold of accumulated distinct-session entropy, meaning fresh accounts start with near-zero weight until they prove varied history. Attackers pay a basalt-hard cost: each duplicate needs months of genuine diverse activity and fresh hardware, making mass sybil creation economically irrational.
